condition: involuntary painful vaginal muscle spasms preventing routine speculum pelvic examination over 2 years
level_rationale: Recurring involuntary painful vaginal muscle spasms that tighten and prevent speculum insertion at routine pelvic smear examinations over 2 years in a 25-year-old indicate primary genito-pelvic penetration disorder warranting pelvic-floor physical therapist or psychosexual therapist desensitization and muscle relaxation therapy, whereas feeling brief mild pressure for 5 seconds during routine smear exams reflects normal speculum sensation requiring no follow-up beyond self-care.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 25, routine pelvic smear exams over 2 years, and involuntary painful vaginal muscle spasms preventing the exam) without naming vaginismus, with an exact 16-vs-16 word span swap and zero stated negatives. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, changing only f3 during the same routine smear exams to brief mild pressure for 5 seconds shifts care cleanly from pelvic-floor or psychosexual therapist treatment (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
